private browser storage and rendering.\\n+`src/pantry.ts` owns item identity, needed choices, session state and save/retry status.\\n+`src/private/storage.ts` owns the local key, JSON validation and the browser storage API.\\n+`src/ui/render.ts` renders snapshots and calls the public pantry interface; rendering can use browser DOM APIs.\\n+The direction is startup to owners, UI to the public pantry contract, and storage to its public types.\\n+No aliases, private re-exports or dynamic dependencies are supported.\\n+Changing the save representation stays in storage; changing labels stays in UI while public contracts hold.\\n+A bundler or UI framework is unnecessary for this small ES-module app; TypeScript emits browser modules with explicit `.js` imports.\\n+\\n+## Acceptance\\n+\\n+Add Rice, mark it needed, view Rice on the shopping list, reload and retain it after successful saving.\\n+Needed is independent of stock; there are no quantities or stock levels.\\n+Trimmed case-insensitive full names reuse the existing item; Brown rice and White rice remain distinct.\\n+Failed saving keeps the session usable, visibly unsaved, with no claim of reload retention.\\n+Retry saves the complete current session and clears the unsaved indicator only after success.\\n+Unmarking removes an item from the shopping list without removing it from the pantry.\\n+Empty names are rejected; invalid saved data is reported rather than trusted, and a new usable session can be saved.\\n+`tests/journey.test.mjs` observes these cases on real Chrome, including DOM output and reload; screenshots go to unique temporary directories.\\n+Its failure injection affects only the disposable browser session.\\n+\\n+## Selected rules and exceptions\\n+\\n+UI storage isolation protects honest retention: UI uses the public pantry interface, never private storage imports or direct localStorage access.\\n+`eslint.config.mjs` is the authoritative executable boundary configuration, scoped to `src/ui/**/*.ts`; native rules leave DOM rendering available.\\n+Static public-only imports, private-import restrictions and localStorage/global-object property restrictions cover the supported syntax.\\n+Arbitrary computed strings, reflection and aliases of browser objects are outside deterministic coverage and require review; do not introduce those bypasses.\\n+There are no selected boundary exceptions; an exception requires an owner decision, narrow scope, reason and removal condition.\\n+The strict compiler protects snapshot and persistence contracts; Prettier owns formatting and ESLint owns lint settings.\\n+The browser journey protects household behavior and honest retention; no unit-only result establishes readiness.\\n+Human review checks that proposed responsibilities serve the vision and that browser assertions derive from this acceptance section.\\n+No speculative service layers, product backend, accounts, hosted CI or remote persistence are introduced.\\n+\\n+## Completion and maintenance\\n+\\n+A change is complete when affected acceptance cases pass on final inputs and its impact on registered authoritative documents has been reviewed.\\n+Root guidance points to the sources; it does not duplicate their rules.\\n+`.bstack/project.json` registers document, rule, command and scope authority; `.bstack/bin/bstack-check.mjs` and its packaged dependencies are the installed dependency-free maintenance runtime.\\n+For routine changes, collect against an explicit ancestor, assess every candidate and unmapped path, review literal source citations and bind current inputs; keep a portable `.bstack/assessment.json` in a separate commit after implementation.\\n+Run the maintained aggregate with Node and Git in the working checkout and a clean different-root clone with isolated home and cache; each invocation runs fresh required leaf checks.\\n+The first contract is authorized by selected foundation finding F-003; do not weaken previous contract coverage silently.\\n+No hosted CI or delivery service is selected; local author review owns semantic approval.\\n--- /dev/null\\n+++ responsibility\\n+This project helps a household remember its named pantry supplies and decide what to buy.\\n+It owns a simple pantry record and a shopping list derived from the household's needed choices.\\n+Version one serves a household locally in a browser, without an account, server or remote service.\\n+These commitments come from the author's approved brief and intent interview, not project history.\\n+\\n+## Household control\\n+An item represents one named pantry supply.\\n+The household explicitly marks which items it needs to buy, independently of whether it already has any stock.\\n+The shopping list contains those needed items.\\n+Accept changes that make those choices easy to record and understand.\\n+Resist changes that substitute inferred inventory decisions for the household's choice.\\n+Quantities and stock levels are outside version one's responsibility.\\n+\\n+## Clear names\\n+Names let the household recognize and distinguish its supplies.\\n+Trim surrounding whitespace and compare full names case-insensitively to reuse an existing item rather than create an accidental duplicate.\\n+Preserve meaningful variants through their full supplied names, such as Brown rice and White rice.\\n+Accept changes that prevent accidental duplicate records without hiding meaningful differences between supplies.\\n+Resist changes that force a product catalogue or complex classification before a household can add an item.\\n+\\n+## Honest retention\\n+The household can add Rice, mark it needed, view it on the shopping list, reload and retain it after successful saving.\\n+Local persistence must communicate whether changes are saved.\\n+When saving fails, keep the current session usable and visibly identify unsaved changes.\\n+Only successful saving establishes reload retention; an unsaved session must never be presented as retained.\\n+Offer a local retry that saves the complete current session, including every current item and needed choice.\\n+Clear the unsaved indicator only after saving succeeds, without sending household data to a remote service.\\n+Accept changes that keep the session useful and make saving problems visible.\\n+Resist changes that promise retention when saving has failed.\\n+\\n+## Boundaries and contribution tests\\n+Version one uses TypeScript and local storage in a local browser.\\n+Accounts, remote synchronization, servers, quantities and stock levels are non-goals.\\n+A change aligns when it strengthens the household's ability to record named supplies, choose what to buy and understand whether its choices will survive reload.\\n+Resist a change when it expands those responsibilities or weakens explicit household control or honest persistence without a new author decision.\\n--- rendering.\\n+`src/pantry.ts` owns item identity, needed choices, session state and save/retry status.\\n+`src/private/storage.ts` owns the local key, JSON validation and the browser storage API.\\n+`src/ui/render.ts` renders snapshots and calls the public pantry interface; rendering can use browser DOM APIs.\\n+The direction is startup to owners, UI to the public pantry contract, and storage to its public types.\\n+No aliases, private re-exports or dynamic dependencies are supported.\\n+Changing the save representation stays in storage; changing labels stays in UI while public contracts hold.\\n+A bundler or UI framework is unnecessary for this small ES-module app; TypeScript emits browser modules with explicit `.js` imports.\\n+\\n+## Acceptance\\n+\\n+Add Rice, mark it needed, view Rice on the shopping list, reload and retain it after successful saving.\\n+Needed is independent of stock; there are no quantities or stock levels.\\n+Trimmed case-insensitive full names reuse the existing item; Brown rice and White rice remain distinct.\\n+Failed saving keeps the session usable, visibly unsaved, with no claim of reload retention.\\n+Retry saves the complete current session and clears the unsaved indicator only after success.\\n+Unmarking removes an item from the shopping list without removing it from the pantry.\\n+Empty names are rejected; invalid saved data is reported rather than trusted, and a new usable session can be saved.\\n+`tests/journey.test.mjs` observes these cases on real Chrome, including DOM output and reload; screenshots go to unique temporary directories.\\n+Its failure injection affects only the disposable browser session.\\n+\\n+## Selected rules and exceptions\\n+\\n+UI storage isolation protects honest retention: UI uses the rules leave DOM rendering available.\\n+Static public-only imports, private-import restrictions and localStorage/global-object property restrictions cover the supported syntax.\\n+Arbitrary computed supplies and decide what to buy.\\n+It owns a simple pantry record and a shopping list derived from the household's needed choices.\\n+Version one serves a household locally in a browser, without an account, server or remote service.\\n+These commitments come from the author's approved brief and intent interview, not project history.\\n+\\n+## Household control\\n+An item represents one named pantry supply.\\n+The household explicitly marks which items it needs to buy, independently of whether it already has any stock.\\n+The shopping list contains those needed items.\\n+Accept changes that make those choices easy to record and understand.\\n+Resist changes that substitute inferred inventory decisions for the household's choice.\\n+Quantities and stock levels are outside version one's responsibility.\\n+\\n+## Clear names\\n+Names let the household recognize and distinguish its supplies.\\n+Trim surrounding whitespace and compare full names case-insensitively to reuse an existing item rather than create an accidental duplicate.\\n+Preserve meaningful variants through their full supplied names, such as Brown rice and White rice.\\n+Accept changes that prevent accidental duplicate records without hiding meaningful differences between supplies.\\n+Resist changes that force a product catalogue or complex classification before a household can add an item.\\n+\\n+## Honest retention\\n+The household can add Rice, mark it needed, view it on the shopping list, reload and retain it after successful saving.\\n+Local persistence must communicate whether changes are saved.\\n+When saving fails, keep the current session usable and visibly identify unsaved changes.\\n+Only successful saving establishes reload retention; an unsaved session must never be presented as retained.\\n+Offer a local retry that saves the complete current session, including every current item and needed choice.\\n+Clear the unsaved indicator only after saving succeeds, without sending household data to a remote service.\\n+Accept changes that keep the session useful and make saving problems visible.\\n+Resist changes that promise retention when saving has failed.\\n+\\n+## Boundaries and contribution tests\\n+Version one uses TypeScript and local storage in a local browser.\\n+Accounts, remote synchronization, servers, quantities and stock levels are non-goals.\\n+A change aligns when it strengthens the household's ability to record named supplies, choose what to buy and understand whether its choices will survive reload.\\n+Resist a change when it expands those responsibilities or weakens explicit household control or honest persistence without a new author decision.\\n--- /dev/null\\n+++ b/eslint.config.mjs\\n@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@\\n+import
